source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt); PDF page 11 items 12 and 13 and the NOTE (total exemptions from all plans under 12 and 13 cannot exceed 6,000 per taxpayer); PDF page 13 LINE 18A and 18B (public or private employment-related plans, the recipient does not have to be retired; traditional IRA after 59 1/2); record ar_employer_plan_exclusion, ar_traditional_ira_exclusion_59_5; Subject 206 page 1 (each spouse has their own 6,000)

worked: Joint, 64 and 60. Primary: federal civil service (OPM) pension 15,000. Spouse: traditional IRA 8,000 and wages 30,000. Each taxpayer has their own 6,000 (line 18A primary, line 18B spouse). Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (spouse) 30,000.00 + traditional IRA distribution (spouse) 8,000.00 + public pension paid by federal (primary) 15,000.00 = 53,000.00. Federal taxable income = 53,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 21,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 2 (married filing joint); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 30,000.00. Line 18A (primary, age 64): gross pension 15,000.00 = 15,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption: exemption = lesser of 15,000.00 and 6,000.00 = 6,000.00; taxable 9,000.00. Line 18B (spouse, age 60): gross traditional IRA after 59 1/2 8,000.00 = 8,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption: exemption = lesser of 8,000.00 and 6,000.00 = 6,000.00; taxable 2,000.00. Line 23 total income = 41,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 41,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 53,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_59_5_plus) 6,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_59_5_plus) 6,000.00 = state AGI 41,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 2) 4,940.00; line 28 net taxable income = 41,000.00 - 4,940.00 = 36,060.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (36,060.00 - 26,400.00) 9,660.00 = 376.74; total 986.38. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 36,001-36,101 gives 986; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 2 = 2 x 29.00 = 58.00; line 7C and line 34 58.00; line 37 total credits 58.00. Line 38 net tax = 986.38 - 58.00 = 928.38. Status 4 would give primary 9,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 6,530.00, tax 2% x 930.00 = 18.60, and spouse 32,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 29,530.00, tax 731.71: together 750.31 before credits, below the joint 986.38; the projection uses status 2 (approximations).
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.

Married couples are taxed on the one table using joint net taxable income (filing status 2). Arkansas also lets them file separately on the same return (status 4, each spouse's tax from the same table on their own income, added), which is lower whenever both have income, because each spouse gets the lower bands.
